## 25.1 The Complete 30-Day Package Launch Sequence

This chapter provides a day-by-day execution plan for building and registering SpatialStats.jl as a production Julia package. The sequence is designed to be executed using Claude Code (the claude CLI) with the specifications developed in this volume, alongside human review and validation at each milestone.


## 25.2 Final Claude Code: Integration Test

```julia
# CLAUDE CODE SPEC: Integration Test After All Packages Built
# File: specs/final_integration_test.md

## Objective
Verify that all six packages work together in a complete
end-to-end rural healthcare geographic analysis workflow.

## Test Scenario
Analyze primary care access in North Dakota counties using:
  - SpatialStats.jl: spatial weights and Moran's I
  - Geocode.jl: geocode provider addresses
  - SpatialReg.jl: spatial lag model of CVD mortality
  - Overpass.jl: download road network
  - MapClassify.jl: classify results for choropleth mapping

## Integration Test Code
# (example: julia)
using SpatialStats, Geocode, MapClassify, Overpass
using DataFrames, CSV, Shapefile, GeoMakie, CairoMakie

# 1. Load North Dakota county boundaries
nd_counties = Shapefile.Table("nd_counties.shp") |> DataFrame

# 2. Build queen contiguity weights
w = queen_weights(nd_counties.geometry)
@assert w.n == 53  # North Dakota has 53 counties
@assert 0.0 < w.mean_neighbors < 8.0

# 3. Load and geocode provider addresses
providers = CSV.read("nd_providers.csv", DataFrame)
g = CensusGeocoder()
geocoded = geocode_all(g, providers; batch_size=500)
@assert !all(ismissing, geocoded.lat)

# 4. Run Moran's I on CVD mortality
cvd_rates = CSV.read("nd_cvd_rates.csv", DataFrame).rate
mi = moran(cvd_rates, w; method=:permutation, permutations=999)
println("Moran's I = $(round(mi.I; digits=4)), p = $(round(mi.p_value; digits=4))")

# 5. Compute LISA cluster map
lisa_result = moran_local(cvd_rates, w)
n_hh = count(==(:HH), lisa_result.cluster)
println("Hot spots (HH clusters): $(n_hh) counties")

# 6. Classify rates for choropleth
breaks = classify(cvd_rates, NaturalBreaks(5))
@assert length(breaks.bins) == 6  # 5 classes = 6 break points

# 7. Download road network from OSM
bbox = (45.9, -104.0, 49.0, -96.5)  # North Dakota extent
osm_xml = download_road_network(bbox; transport=:drive)
@assert length(osm_xml) > 100  # Non-empty XML returned

# 8. Draw LISA cluster map
fig = Figure(resolution=(1200,800))
ga  = GeoAxis(fig[1,1];
    dest  = "+proj=laea +lat_0=47 +lon_0=-100",
    title = "CVD Mortality LISA Clusters — North Dakota")

cluster_colors = Dict(:HH=>:red, :LL=>:blue, :HL=>:orange,
                       :LH=>:lightblue, :NS=>:white)
colors = [cluster_colors[c] for c in lisa_result.cluster]
poly!(ga, nd_counties.geometry;
    color=colors, strokecolor=:black, strokewidth=0.5)
save("nd_lisa_map.pdf", fig)

println("\n✓ All integration tests passed.")
println("✓ SpatialStats.jl: weights + autocorrelation")
println("✓ Geocode.jl: address geocoding")
println("✓ MapClassify.jl: natural breaks classification")
println("✓ Overpass.jl: road network download")
println("✓ GeoMakie.jl: LISA cluster map rendered")
# (end example)

END — Volume III: Julia Geospatial Package Engineering — 2026 Edition
```
